draft.title: Cross-surface consistency diff
draft.principle_summary: A design token being individually valid at every call site does not guarantee the same semantic role renders the same value everywhere. Nielsen's "consistency and standards" heuristic (his 4th of 10, derived from a factor analysis of 249 logged usability problems, refined 1994, NN/g) names the failure mode: sticking to the same word, situation, or visual treatment for the same concept throughout a product, both internally (this product) and externally (platform convention). Gestalt similarity, already load-bearing in RATIONALE.md's Twin-control rule, is the perceptual mechanism: identical form is the cue that tells the eye two elements are the same kind of thing, and styling two instances of one semantic role differently breaks that signal even though each instance, taken alone, may sit inside the locked token set. D7 turns "this feels inconsistent" into a computable divergence report instead of a vibe.

draft.solen_current: RATIONALE.md section 28 (Gap register) already names this gap verbatim at row D7 ("Cross-surface consistency diff (price strings, stroke widths, twin components across call-sites)") and marks it Mechanizable = YES, but it is an unstarted line item, not a spec. The Twin-control rule (RATIONALE.md:368-373, grounding LOCKFILE:435-437) states the PRINCIPLE (two controls sharing one purpose must be the same styled instance) but gives no procedure for detecting a violation across an arbitrary number of call sites; it reads as a bare assertion enforceable only by a reviewer noticing by eye. solen-drift-check (.claude/skills/solen-drift-check/SKILL.md) is the only mechanized checker that exists today, and by its own stated scope it operates per-file against a fixed allowlist of legal literals (A1 hex, A2 arbitrary Tailwind, A3 duration, A4 easing, A5 retired token); it cannot catch the case in the key_question, where a card in Hero renders rounded-[18px] and a card in Footer renders rounded-2xl (16px) and a third renders rounded-[22px], because none of those three literals individually breaks a single-file rule (18 and 22 are outside the six locked radius steps and WOULD be caught by A2 if written as bracket values, but a component that quietly reads a prop and resolves to rounded-lg (a real Tailwind class, not a bracket literal) would slip through entirely). The commit history in this worktree (c21c6cd91: "status filter pills off banned ink-fill selected onto locked TabPill gray") shows this exact failure mode landing in production code and only getting caught by manual B9 render verification, not by any script.
draft.gap: D7 is unmechanized. The gap is not "no rule exists" (the Twin-control rule and the TabPill/radius locks already state the target values); the gap is "no procedure exists to prove two-plus call sites of the same semantic role agree", which is exactly the failure mode that produced the c21c6cd91 fix (TabPill ink-fill drift caught by eye during a screenshot review, not by a script) and the key_question's SalonResultCard/Hero/Footer/Header radius example. Per-file allowlist checking (solen-drift-check) structurally cannot see this: consistency is a property of a SET of call sites for one role, not a property of any single file.
draft.proposed_addition:
COMPUTABLE METRIC SPEC, D7: Cross-surface consistency diff.

INPUTS
1. A ROLE REGISTRY: a hand-maintained list mapping a semantic role name to (a) a glob/regex of call-site files that render it, (b) the CSS property or Tailwind class family that carries the role's visual value, and (c) the canonical/locked value where LOCKFILE names one, or "CONV: mode-wins" where it does not. Seed entries, pulled directly from the LOCKFILE rows already frozen (no new literal proposed, only named for diffing):
   - role "card-radius": call sites = any component whose className applies rounded-2xl, rounded-lg, rounded-[NNpx], or a radius prop, restricted to files tagged card/panel; canonical = 16px (rounded-2xl), per LOCKFILE:414-426.
   - role "tabpill-selected-fill": call sites = TabPill.tsx plus any component that renders a pill/chip/segment with a "selected" boolean; extraction target = the className branch taken when selected is true; canonical = bg-s-bg-sunken + text-s-ink + font-semibold, per CLAUDE.md design-contract row "selected / active" (2026-06-29).
   - role "price-string-format": call sites = every component rendering a CHF amount; extraction target = the literal format string or template around the number; canonical = the format already locked at LOCKFILE:772-778,793 per RATIONALE.md's "Service-row format and price-string convention" entry.
   - role "icon-stroke-width": call sites = every component importing a Lucide icon with a strokeWidth prop; canonical = the value named in RATIONALE.md's "Icon stroke width inconsistency" entry (LOCKFILE:1218,1279-1280), itself flagged there as unresolved, so this role starts as CONV: mode-wins until the owner locks one number.
   Additional roles get added the same way: name it, name its call sites, name its canonical value or mark it CONV.

2. EXTRACTION: for each role, grep/AST-walk every call-site file for the property's literal value (a px number resolved from the Tailwind class, a hex, a class-name string, a format-string shape), tagged with file:line. This reuses the same AST/regex machinery solen-drift-check already has (scripts/check.py), pointed at a role's call-site set instead of at a single changed file.

FORMULA
- For a role R with N call sites, extract the multiset of values V = {v1..vN}.
- distinct_count(R) = number of unique values in V.
- mode(R) = the most frequent value in V (ties broken toward the LOCKFILE canonical value if one is named).
- divergence_rate(R) = count(vi != mode(R)) / N.
- outliers(R) = the list of (file, line, value) pairs where vi != mode(R).

THRESHOLDS
- distinct_count(R) == 1: PASS, no output line.
- distinct_count(R) >= 2 AND R has a LOCKFILE-named canonical value: every vi != canonical is a HARD finding (contract breach, same severity class as an A1-A5 solen-drift-check hit; D10's severity matrix already names this tier "contract breach = blocking regardless of visual size"). This is the TabPill ink-fill case and the key_question's radius case when the canonical is 16px.
- distinct_count(R) >= 2 AND R has no LOCKFILE-named canonical (CONV: mode-wins roles): every vi != mode(R) is a SOFT finding (cosmetic/informational, logged not gated), because there is no locked ground truth to breach, only an internal-inconsistency signal (the Nielsen T1 mechanic above, not a literal contract).
- divergence_rate(R) reported per role regardless of severity, so "20% of card call sites disagree with the canonical" replaces "this feels inconsistent" with a number.

WHAT IT FLAGS
- The exact key_question scenario: SalonResultCard/Hero/Footer/Header each independently valid as a Tailwind class or in-token literal, but disagreeing with each other on the SAME role. solen-drift-check's per-file allowlist cannot see this because no single file's value is illegal in isolation; D7 sees it because it groups by role across files first.
- Regressions of an already-fixed drift (the TabPill ink-fill case in c21c6cd91): once tabpill-selected-fill's canonical is registered, any future call site reintroducing bg-s-ink on a selected pill becomes a HARD finding on the next run, not a manual screenshot catch.

HOW IT MAPS A VAGUE COMPLAINT TO A NUMBER
Owner says "the cards feel inconsistent across the site." Run D7 scoped to role card-radius: output is a table of file:line -> value, a mode, a divergence_rate, and a named canonical if one exists. The reply becomes "Header.tsx:42 renders rounded-[18px], 4 other card call sites render rounded-2xl (16px, the locked value); divergence_rate = 20%; Header is the sole outlier" instead of "yes it does feel off, let me look."

BOUNDARY: this spec defines inputs/formula/thresholds only, no code is written here per the task constraint. Building it means extending scripts/check.py (or a sibling script) with a role registry and a group-by-role pass; it is additive to solen-drift-check, not a replacement, and should ship as a new mode (e.g. --cross-surface) rather than folding into the existing per-file gate, since its unit of analysis (a role's call-site set) differs from the existing gate's unit (one file's diff).
draft.taste_lab_probe: Not applicable to a mechanize-tag stream: D7 is a build-ready metric spec, not a generative prior needing owner calibration. The one open input that DOES need an owner decision before the icon-stroke-width role can move from CONV to HARD-checkable is naming the single canonical strokeWidth value (RATIONALE.md already flags this as unresolved at LOCKFILE:1218,1279-1280); that is a one-line owner pick, not a probe.

verified.residual_risks:
Two items for the owner, neither a change to a frozen literal:

1. icon-stroke-width canonicalization: RATIONALE.md itself flags LOCKFILE:1218,1279-1280 as internally inconsistent (1.9 vs 2, "reconcile" note already present). D7's role registry can only move this role from CONV (soft findings) to HARD (contract-breach findings) once the owner picks one stroke-width number. This is a QUESTIONS.md candidate, not something this spec should resolve by picking a value itself.

2. The one overclaim caught in this pass (solen-drift-check's doesn't-catch list not literally naming the cross-file scenario) was a framing issue, not a factual error in the underlying mechanics, and has been softened in verified_addition. No frozen literal was touched or reopened by this correction.

No myth-table numbers were present in the original draft, so nothing needed to be cut on that front. The spec's own severity-matrix dependency (D10, "contract breach = blocking regardless of visual size") is referenced but D10 itself is a separate unstarted gap-register line; D7's HARD/SOFT split assumes D10 lands with compatible severity semantics, worth a one-line owner confirmation when both are scheduled for build.
